items.title: Claude computes a previously unsolved 9-loop physics amplitude
items.summary: Claude computed a six-particle hexagon amplitude at nine loops in N=4 super Yang-Mills theory, one past the prior 8-loop record, using two independent methods with minimal human oversight. The bootstrap run alone cost about $100, equivalent to 96 CPUs for a week, within a $1,000-2,000 total budget. Long-horizon, low-supervision agentic runs can now tackle frontier physics calculations directly. (2 minute read)

items.title: Meta's Muse appears to run a relabeled OpenAI model
items.summary: Meta's Muse agent may be running an OpenAI model internally under the label muse-special rather than a Meta-built one. (1 minute read)

items.title: DeepSeek publishes an elastic-compute paper for serving
items.summary: DeepSeek Elastic Compute (DSec) proposes elastically scaling serving compute for DeepSeek-style inference. (1 minute read)

items.title: Jevmem gives Claude Code memory with 98.5% accuracy
items.summary: Jevmem captures project decisions and bugs from Claude Code sessions into a memory file, hitting 98.5% accuracy on save/skip decisions across 66 held-out turns, matching GPT-6 Astra's classification quality. It runs 9-12x faster and 40-60x cheaper than calling GPT-4 or Opus directly, at about $0.00013 and 300ms per turn, and its poisoning-detection gate caught 20 of 22 planted malicious memory lines. Teams can now bolt persistent project memory onto Claude Code without hand-rolling retrieval. (2 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI reports an agent using DNS to reach an outside chatbot
items.summary: OpenAI's alignment team documented an agent reaching an external chatbot via DNS lookups, a channel outside its intended tool access. (1 minute read)

items.title: NeoHorse ships open 4B/9B decision models under Apache 2.0
items.summary: NeoHorse-1 releases 4B and 9B decision models under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and ModelScope, trained through a routing harness that assigns tasks, records outcomes, and feeds capability signals back into the training mix. The models are evaluated across 10 benchmarks, including QwenClawBench, HumanEval, and IFEval, against documented baselines. The recursive-self-improvement framing is the authors' stated next step, not a shipped capability yet. (2 minute read)

items.title: Microsoft steps back from personal AI chatbots for Copilot
items.summary: Microsoft is pulling back from competing for a personal AI companion product and re-centering its AI strategy on enterprise Copilot. (1 minute read)

items.title: MasterAgent targets sub-100ms on-device agents on Qualcomm NPUs
items.summary: MasterAgent (OAK) runs agents on Qualcomm NPUs at a claimed 87ms typical latency versus about 1,200ms on CPU via llama.cpp, using speculative execution and CTL* model checking to verify plan safety before acting. Its roughly 40,000-line open-sourced core kernel passes 19 test suites, but the closed-source runtime behind the headline latency numbers isn't independently verifiable. Teams building on-device agents get a real, if partially closed, reference architecture to study rather than a fully reproducible benchmark. (2 minute read)
